Section 748(b)(3)(B) (42 U.S.C. 294e(b)(3)(B)) is amended (1) by striking out “or” at the end of clause (iv), (2) by striking out the period at the end of clause (v) and inserting in lieu thereof “, or”, and (3) by adding after clause (v) the following:


“(vi) maternal and child health.”.



 
    (b) 
Section 792(a) (42 U.S.C. 295h–1(a)) is amended (1) by striking out “or” at the end of paragraph (3), (2) by striking out the period at the end of paragraph (4) and inserting in lieu thereof “, or”, and (3) by adding after paragraph (4) the following new paragraph:


“(vi) maternal and child health.”.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments that add "maternal and child health" to existing lists in two statutory provisions. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue that would bring a party outside the federal government into a federal decision. There is no tempting participation language here at all.

opus.w: This section only makes technical amendments that add "maternal and child health" to existing statutory lists. It does not require or allow consultation with anyone outside the federal government, and it creates no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. Any link to grant programs doesn't count, because applying for grants is excluded from participation.

opus.b:
I'd label this **No**. Both subsections are technical, clerical amendments: they add "maternal and child health" as a new item at the end of lists in 42 U.S.C. 294e(b)(3)(B) and 42 U.S.C. 295h-1(a).

The only tempting reading is that these sections belong to Public Health Service Act programs about health training grants, so adding a field might seem to bring outside parties in. But applying for grants is excluded under the definition. Nothing in this text creates a comment period, hearing, rulemaking authority, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends a list of eligible health categories by adding 'maternal and child health.' It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or interaction with outside parties (such as states, tribes, experts, or the public) before a federal decision is made. The text defines the scope of the program but does not establish a participatory process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that adding "maternal and child health" to a list of eligible areas implies that the government will consult with maternal and child health experts or organizations. However, the text itself only amends the statutory list of eligible categories; it does not mandate any specific consultation, hearing, or advisory process involving outside parties. The definition requires that the section *itself* involve participation (consultation, coordination, advisory boards with non-federal members, etc.). Merely defining the scope of a program or listing eligible topics does not constitute participation.
